paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss steps
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of large language models, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and multiple configurations of StrmLLM and SepLLM with different segment sizes (n=64 and n=128) and optional hierarchical or hybrid training strategies (H, H/T). The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 in linear scale with major tick marks every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 in linear scale, with tick marks at 0.1 intervals. All curves begin near a loss of 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep decline in the first 20,000 iterations, followed by a gradual flattening toward convergence. The “Vanilla” model (purple, solid line) consistently shows the lowest loss across iterations, ending near 2.5 at 140,000 iterations. The “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue, solid line) starts slightly higher and converges near 2.6. The “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange, solid line) and “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green, solid line) follow closely, ending near 2.55 and 2.53 respectively. The “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red, solid line) and “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue, solid line) show slightly higher final losses, around 2.57 and 2.62 respectively, indicating a modest performance trade-off for the compression techniques. All lines are smooth with no visible markers, suggesting continuous or averaged loss values over training steps.
